events.extended_summary: The Trump administration announced plans to impose new trade tariffs on 14 major trading partners, including China, the European Union and India, accusing them of flooding world markets with cheap goods through structural excess capacity. China faces the highest rates. The Office of the US Trade Representative announced the duties following an eight-month investigation, imposing them under Section 301 of the 1974 US trade law. The tariffs are the latest attempt to rebuild sweeping import taxes that the US Supreme Court struck down in February. The rates are not due to come in until January or February after consultation and will largely replace previous findings on forced labour provisions. The UK remains unaffected by the new announcement but stays subject to 10 percent tariffs under forced labour provisions. Twenty-five states have taken the administration to court over the forced labour tariffs.
events.micro_summary: The Trump administration announced new tariffs on 14 trading partners including China and the EU under Section 301.
events.summary: The Trump administration announced new trade tariffs on 14 major partners including China, the EU and India under Section 301, with China facing the highest rates, to replace tariffs struck down by the Supreme Court.

events.extended_summary: On November 25, 2026, at approximately 9:00 a.m. CST, the U.S. Army conducted a controlled detonation of nearly five tonnes of unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa. The explosives had been stored for around 20 years and degraded through recrystallisation, risking accidental detonation. Residents within a five-mile zone southwest of the plant were evacuated starting November 24, with FEMA providing transportation, shelter, and meals through November 27. Smoke rose after the blast, but officials declared the risk 'as close to zero as is absolutely humanly possible' and reported no lead readings above 0.0. President Donald Trump said mitigation efforts 'far exceeded expectations,' and acting Army Secretary Adam Telle called the operation a 'HUGE success.' Middletown Mayor Rodney Johnson expressed relief, noting residents eight miles away felt nothing.
events.micro_summary: The U.S. Army detonated nearly five tonnes of unstable lead azide in Iowa on November 25, 2026.
events.summary: The U.S. Army detonated nearly five tonnes of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on November 25, 2026, after evacuating residents within a five-mile zone; officials reported success with no lead readings above 0.0.

events.extended_summary: Estonia will close all road border crossings with Russia from December 1 for at least six months, halting land traffic at the Narva-Ivangorod crossing. Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna cited Russia's aggressive behavior, including a suspected arson attack on drone company Threod Systems near Tallinn, as the trigger. Tsahkna warned Russia has been "boiling Europe as a frog." Russia's Foreign Ministry lodged a formal protest, accusing Estonia of hostile actions putting it "on the verge of unleashing open war" and imposing a naval blockade. Estonia denied these claims, stating it never allows its territory for military operations and that Russia is diverting attention from its own attacks on European security, citing missile strikes on Poland and an assassination plot in Denmark. Estonia shares a 294-kilometer border with Russia.
events.micro_summary: Estonia closes its border with Russia from December 1 for at least six months.
events.summary: Estonia will close all land border crossings with Russia from December 1 for at least six months, citing aggressive Russian actions including a suspected arson attack on a drone company, while Russia accuses Estonia of hostile actions risking open war.

events.extended_summary: China launched the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft on Wednesday at 08:18 local time from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre, carrying Pakistan's first astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali alongside Chinese commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer Wu Yi. The Long March-2F rocket lifted off at 00:18 GMT, and the spacecraft docked with the Tiangong space station at 8:56am (03:56 GMT). Ali, a 40-year-old Pakistan Air Force pilot, will conduct experiments on photosynthesis in bacteria and the effects of radiation and microgravity on seeds before returning to Earth after a short stay. Tang and Wu will remain at the station for six months with Zhu Yangzhu. The mission marks the first time a foreign astronaut has joined a Chinese crewed mission and coincides with 75 years of space cooperation between China and Pakistan.
events.micro_summary: China launched the Shenzhou-24 mission carrying Pakistan's first astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali to the Tiangong space station.
events.summary: China launched the Shenzhou-24 mission from Jiuquan carrying Pakistan's first astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and two Chinese crew members to the Tiangong space station, where the spacecraft docked successfully hours later.

events.extended_summary: Unknown attackers breached an open-source intelligence analysis system at the CIA, also affecting the Office of the Director of National Intelligence and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, using the ARTEX AI-powered penetration testing framework. No classified data or systems were exposed and there were no disruptions to critical capabilities. Early indications suggest the hack may have originated in China, though government involvement remains unclear. Separately, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network disclosed unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems, took some systems offline as a precaution, and is working with the FBI and CISA to determine the scope, with no evidence of breaches to beneficial ownership databases or the Bank Secrecy Act.
events.micro_summary: Unknown attackers breached CIA and ODNI intelligence systems using AI tools, but no classified data was exposed.
events.summary: Unknown attackers breached an open-source intelligence system at the CIA, ODNI and National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency using the ARTEX AI framework, though no classified data was exposed; FinCEN also disclosed unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems.

events.extended_summary: A survey of 1,827 UK adults conducted in March 2026 reveals widespread misperceptions about immigration, with only 4% correctly identifying that net migration fell significantly between 2024 and 2025, while nearly two-thirds believed it had risen. Net migration has fallen, following a two-thirds drop in the year to June 2025. The public also overestimates support for immigration cuts and mistakenly believes asylum seekers outnumber students and their dependants. However, respondents accurately estimated that 18% of the UK population was born abroad, matching official data of 18.9%, and 71% correctly recognized asylum seekers cannot work immediately. Most know asylum seekers can access free NHS and dental care during processing. These misperceptions correlate with firmer anti-immigration attitudes and policy preferences across political groups.
events.micro_summary: Only 4% of UK adults correctly recognize that net migration fell significantly between 2024 and 2025.
events.summary: A survey of 1,827 UK adults finds widespread misperceptions about immigration, with only 4% correctly stating net migration fell significantly between 2024 and 2025 while nearly two-thirds believed it rose.

events.extended_summary: Usman Khawaja has said he was hurt by personal attacks from Australia Test captain Pat Cummins after Cummins disputed Khawaja's claims that every member of the side was aware of the use of sandpaper during the 2018 ball-tampering scandal in South Africa. Khawaja made the allegations in his autobiography Sabr, and they have since been backed by David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, who along with then-skipper Steve Smith received bans following the incident. Cummins, who was part of the bowling attack on that tour, insisted he was not aware of the scheme when he and fellow bowlers Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon released a joint statement in 2021. Cummins categorically denied knowledge in a 68-minute press conference earlier this month, accusing Khawaja of being casual with people's lives. Khawaja expressed surprise at Cummins' response, having hoped the captain would bring the team together.
events.micro_summary: Usman Khawaja says Pat Cummins' personal attacks hurt him over 2018 sandpaper claims.

sources.publisher: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation

events.summary: Usman Khawaja stated he was hurt by Pat Cummins' personal attacks after the Australia captain denied claims that all team members knew of the 2018 sandpaper use, which Khawaja made in his autobiography and Warner and Bancroft supported.

events.extended_summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers benched quarterback Aaron Rodgers for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos, naming Mason Rudolph the starter. The decision was announced Tuesday night at 11:10 p.m. ET without explanation, despite Rodgers taking all first-team repetitions during Tuesday's practice. Rodgers stated he learned of the benching through a phone call with tight end Pat Freiermuth rather than from head coach Mike McCarthy, claiming the topic never arose in their conversations. He alleged McCarthy missed meetings and fell asleep during a quarterback meeting, citing disagreements over offensive play-calling. Rodgers declared, "At this point, I'm not going back to Pittsburgh." His brother Jordan Rodgers suggested general manager Omar Khan may have influenced the decision. The move follows the team's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
events.micro_summary: Pittsburgh Steelers bench Aaron Rodgers for Friday's game against Broncos, starting Mason Rudolph instead.
events.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers benched quarterback Aaron Rodgers for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos, naming Mason Rudolph the starter. Rodgers learned of the decision via a phone call with Pat Freiermuth and stated he will not return to Pittsburgh.

events.extended_summary: Heading into Thanksgiving week, all 32 NFL teams remain mathematically alive for the playoffs. Simulations of the remaining 109 regular-season games of the 2026 season project 14 playoff teams. The projected AFC field includes the Bills (9-1), Broncos (8-2), Bengals (7-3), Jaguars (7-3), Chiefs (8-2), Steelers (6-4), and Browns (6-4), with the Texans and Patriots just missing. The Bills-Chiefs Thanksgiving game holds significant implications for the top seed and first-round bye. The Arizona Cardinals could theoretically be eliminated by the end of Week 12 but likely will not be. In the NFC, the 49ers lead toward the top seed while all four NFC North teams remain in the projected field alongside the Rams and Seahawks. The Steelers remain projected for playoffs despite benching Aaron Rodgers. The Jaguars hold the league's best point differential at plus-125.

events.extended_summary: Divers recovered bodies from fuselage after aircraft went down in the Gulf of Mexico A family of six including two children and a teenager died after a plane crashed off the coast of Mississippi, killing everyone on board. The air traffic control regional tower in Mobile, Alabama, reported at about 3.45pm local time that it had lost contact with the aircraft, according to the Coast Guard. Responders searched for hours and initially only found three life jackets, a life raft and the plane’s cabin floating on the water, according to Juan Ros, a Coast Guard spokesman. Divers found the bodies of the victims in the fuselage after the Cessna 210 went down in the Gulf of Mexico between Pascagoula, Mississippi, and Horn Island, which is part of the Gulf Islands National Seashore. The plane’s pilot was Brent Stokes, the 50-year-old president of a marine contracting company based in Fort Myers.
events.micro_summary: Two children among six dead after plane crash off Mississippi coast.
events.summary: Two children among six dead after plane crash off Mississippi coast. Six people, including two children, have been found dead after a plane crashed off the coast of Mississippi on Tuesday, the US Coast Guard says.

events.extended_summary: Former Sydney police officer Beau Lamarre, 31, was found guilty on Wednesday of murdering his former partner Jesse Baird, a 26-year-old TV presenter, and Baird's new partner Luke Davies, 29, with his work-issued gun. The murders occurred in February 2024 at a Sydney home, where CCTV captured Lamarre dressed as an UberEats rider dawdling for 20 minutes before gunshots rang out. During a two-month trial, jurors heard evidence that Lamarre had planned the killings over months, purchasing a surfboard bag to transport Baird's body and later driving the decomposing bodies in a white hire van to a rural property with a dam, where Taylor Swift's "No Body, No Crime" played. The bloodied belongings of the victims were found in a skip in Cronulla, leading to the discovery of their partially buried bodies on a rural property. Lamarre pleaded not guilty, claiming self-defense, but was convicted of both murders.
events.micro_summary: Former Sydney policeman Beau Lamarre, 31, was found guilty of double murder of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies.

events.extended_summary: Relatives of those being held hostage spent anxious hours as the situation unfolded Colombian security forces have freed around 76 shoppers and employees who had been held hostage for about 17 hours at a supermarket in the city of Cartagena. Gunmen had stormed into the building at 08:00 local time (13:00 GMT) on Tuesday after what Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella described as a failed attempt at robbing an armoured car carrying money. They held those inside at gunpoint while trying to negotiate their getaway. With the situation becoming ever more intense as the day progressed, de la Espriella gave the green light for special forces and police to launch a daring operation to free the hostages, killing one gunman. Residents living near the supermarket reported hearing explosions as the security forces moved into the building. Police later confirmed that officers had used stun grenades to overpower the hostage-takers.
events.micro_summary: Colombian police storm supermarket to free 76 held hostage for 17 hours.

events.extended_summary: Union Minister of State for Science and Technology Dr Jitendra Singh announced at the CII Global Genomics Summit 2026 in New Delhi that India's bio-economy is projected to reach $300 billion by 2030. The bio-economy has grown from approximately $10 billion in 2014 to nearly $195 billion at present, while the biotechnology startup ecosystem expanded from around 50-60 startups in 2014 to nearly 11,000. Dr Singh described biotechnology as a key driver of the next industrial revolution and a strategic technology platform with applications across healthcare, agriculture and economic development. He highlighted the Genome India Project, which has undertaken whole-genome sequencing of 10,000 individuals representing 80 population groups, and emphasized the potential of advanced genomic applications in improving crop productivity, livestock breeding and personalised healthcare. The minister also referenced the government's BioE3 Policy aimed at promoting biotechnology for economy, environment and employment.
events.micro_summary: India's bio-economy is projected to reach $300 billion by 2030, driven by biotechnology startups and research expansion.

events.extended_summary: The Indian government has stated it sees no contradiction between Sarvam AI's indigenous AI model development supported by the IndiaAI Mission and the company's new enterprise offering of open-source-based AI models, including Chinese ones. Ministry of Electronics and IT Secretary S Krishnan said on Wednesday that hosting open-weight models to provide AI services from India does not violate IndiaAI Mission principles or misuse incentives. Sarvam launched Token Factory on November 16, an inference stack serving its own 105-billion-parameter model and leading open-weight models including DeepSeek, Kimi, and GLM from GPU clusters in India. While critics questioned how offering Chinese models fit with India's sovereign AI push, Krishnan defended the move, noting AI companies require revenue models. The government continues supporting Sarvam's work toward a trillion-parameter model under the ₹10,372 crore IndiaAI Mission.
events.micro_summary: Government says Sarvam AI hosting Chinese models does not violate IndiaAI Mission as it builds indigenous 105-billion-parameter model.

events.extended_summary: Researchers at IIT Guwahati have developed a new method for assessing seismic hazards in earthquake-prone Northeast India by compiling a catalogue of nearly 6,000 earthquakes recorded over the past 1,200 years and generating 200 synthetic earthquake catalogues. Using Kernel Density Estimation and accounting for geological fault orientations, the study addresses non-uniform seismic activity and historical data inaccuracies. The research identified the Indo-Burma Ranges as having the most intense earthquake activity, with Imphal showing the highest estimated ground shaking among eight major cities including Guwahati, Agartala, Shillong, Aizawl, Kohima, Gangtok and Itanagar. The findings provide crucial information for engineers to design earthquake-resistant buildings, bridges and infrastructure in the vulnerable region between two tectonic boundaries that was devastated by the 1897 Shillong and 1950 Assam earthquakes.
events.micro_summary: IIT Guwahati study of 6,000 earthquakes finds Imphal has highest ground shaking among eight northeastern cities.
events.summary: Researchers at IIT Guwahati developed a new seismic hazard assessment method using nearly 6,000 historical earthquakes over 1,200 years, finding Imphal faces the highest estimated ground shaking among eight major northeastern cities to aid earthquake-resistant construction.
